editorial.brief: The World Cup is the day's dominant cross-feed story, appearing on both Wikipedia and Polymarket, where bettors have put $38 million on Cristiano Ronaldo crying and are pricing Kylian Mbappé to score. Wikipedia's actual top read, though, was Arthur Fery, ahead of Erling Haaland by just 1.4 times, for reasons no other feed explains. Mitch McConnell, meanwhile, is trending on Lemmy and Wikipedia at once, an odd pairing the World Cup can't account for.
editorial.cover_sub: Arthur Fery topped Wikipedia's reading list by the narrowest of margins, edging out Erling Haaland and a World Cup field that otherwise owns four of the day's five most-read pages.
editorial.wiki_deck: 597,106 people read about Arthur Fery today, only 1.4 times more than read about Erling Haaland — and nothing in the day's data says why.
editorial.letter_headline: One Thin Margin, One Genuine Cluster
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News weighs GPT-5.6 against the EU's Chat Control vote; Lemmy trades roses-and-immune-system memes; Bluesky drifts from World Cup fandom to a father finishing The Hobbit; Mastodon is furious Chat Control passed on a losing vote.
editorial.foreign_deck: Asian markets retreated despite an AI rally on Wall Street, Microsoft trimmed its workforce, and four countries searched footballers' names ahead of France versus Morocco.
editorial.markets_deck: Bettors put $38 million on Ronaldo crying at the World Cup, treated as a near-certainty, while France sits at 62 percent against Morocco and Ethiopia's next prime minister at zero.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 held 1.28 million concurrent players, PUBG and Dota 2 followed behind it, and Twitch's biggest room was GamesDoneQuick's marathon with 37,048 watching alongside zackrawrr and Inoxtag.
editorial.yt_note: Dune: Part Three's trailer topped ten million views, more than the other four trending videos combined, ahead of a Godzilla teaser, two music videos, and a gaming strategy clip.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow, Arthur Fery's lead will likely have evaporated into whatever explains it, or vanished for good. GamesDoneQuick's marathon ends, Twitch's numbers reset. wiki_paras: Arthur Fery led Wikipedia's most-read list on Thursday with 597,106 views, ahead of Erling Haaland's 439,920. The gap was 1.4 times — thin, by the standards of a genuine runaway story.
